comment: Professor was very caring and knowledgeable a out the topic. I took this as an elective and did find some of the information to be a little boring but overall I enjoyed the class. We did a bunch of out of class activities and field trips which were cool. Midterm and final exam contained a LOT of terms that you had to know, but overall manageable.

Dr. Baughan is very nice, you can tell she is brilliant+passionate about what she does. Very responsive and flexible. Just be prepared to actually engage with reading/participation because it adheres to grade. Can sort-of get away though without reading though, but makes things more difficult.
Lectures can be dull, but overall she is amazing
She's great. Super easy to reach, and wants to help you learn and be engaged.
Very passionate, but FYS is way too hard. Heavy reading and other homeworks but overall a decent FYS. Just hard.
LOVED her. Such a kind and brilliant woman.

Professor Baughan is an amazing teacher. She is clearly passionate about Classical Studies and everything within the subject. If you are interested in that field, take her class as you will learn a lot and explore different areas. However, you will read a decent amount and participation matters a lot.

She seems like a really nice and caring prof, but her lectures were pretty boring and just repeats of the past nights reading. Lots of small assignments due and bi weekly quizzes which cause undue stress. Would be interesting material except its all ancient pottery upon ancient pottery so is pretty dull and hard to engage with.

I took her Intro to Archaeology class. She is such a sweet person and very passionate about the subject. She assigns text book readings before almost every class, but you can get away with not reading any. The homework is pretty easy and interesting. She also does hands on activities during class and she really wants you to be engaged and get an A.

I did this class only for the gen ed requirement and it definitely was not a subject I cared about. That being said, Dr. Baughan is a really lovely teacher, and made the subject interesting because she cares so much about it.

Professor Baughan is one of the most interesting and passionate teachers I've had. That being said, her FYS is mostly comprised of Classics (like Plato, etc) The reading is copious and hard to understand at times. She is a tough grader on papers. For example, she takes off points if you begin a sentence with "this". Meet with her outside of class!

I had Professor Baughan for my Wining and Dining in the Ancient Mediterranean FYS and the class itself was fairly easy and she is a total sweetheart. The only complaint was that there was anywhere from 1-3 hours of reading in total to prepare for each class, but you can get away with not doing them sometimes. She is very passionate and very nice

Really nice professor. She won't make you feel stupid when you get the answer wrong and will work with you to help you improve. You have a weekly quiz and a few tests. Participation is very important.

She is a great professor! She is really passionate about Archaeology and the best part is that she has a lot of experience in field work and teaching. Classes are really chill and the work load is manageable. She is really helpful even outside class and is really welcoming and energetic. She takes the class out of the classroom setting a lot!

Unless you are deeply interested in classics, do not take this course for your general art requirement. Lectures are dense and require copious note-taking. The paper and creative project are doable, but her tests are especially tough. For the final, expect to memorize 100+ art pieces, their creators, dates, locations, and explain their significance

Prof. Baughan is one of the nicest, most inspirational professors I have had the pleasure of taking. She is a tough grader, but is more than happy to read and critique any paper before you submit it. The class was extremely interesting and I would definitely take it again if I had to do it all over!

I took her Death and Commemoration FYS and it was amazing! I had almost no background in classics and had a really great time. There is an average amount of reading for an FYS, but you don't have to do all of it to get a good grade (A/A-). It does help if you know how to write and present well. One of my favorite professors at UR.

Great teacher! Every class is a lecture so it can get a little boring, but the material is interesting and she is awkwardly funny. There is a lot of reading, so be prepared to work hard. But she will go out of your way to help you, she is really nice and easy-going and just a great prof. in general.

Baughan is a nice professor but she gets very frus. when you do notunderstandthe material She expects youtomemorize latin and constructions for a quiz EVERY monday We had two booksand she only used one what a waste of money to buy the second one She is nice but the class is not unless your a classics major stay away from theclassand latiningeneral

Prof. Baughan is very nice and knowledgeable in her field but the class was ridiculous. It was basically all memorization and reading and she expects well analyzed papers on artifacts in a thoughtful way. I took this as an art credit, big mistake. However, if your focus is classics, then you might want to consider it. Personally, if wasn't for me.

Professor Baughan is one of the nicest professors you'll have, and she is genuinely interested in the topics she teaches. Sometimes the workload can be difficult- prepare yourself for a lot of reading! But the classes are easy and interesting, and she's always willing to help.
